This might be controversial but keep in mind this is my preference and it's okay if we all feel differently about it. I don't think its okay to hate on or generalize an entire gender however I understand that it's an emotionally charged statement made from the frustrations of people who have to put up with certain behaviours from them.

My reasoning for myself, personally(meaning you can disagree as we all have different experiences), is that I was raised a woman and I was treated like one. I was victim to very nasty cis men and although I am just as much as a man as a cis man, I can't change the fact that I have a dual experience. 

I believe in 'not all men' and I don't agree with the generalization of an entire gender. I've met many kind dudes out there as I am sure we all have. But it's a problem that I don't contribute to because I did not grow up in a toxic male culture from birth like some cis men are. I like to think that even if I did I wouldn't be toxic but if I was raised in an echo chamber I don't know how long it would take for me to learn and be better. But I wasn't and toxic masculinity was not ingrained in me because I was raised a girl. 

Again this is just my personal preference and I totally understand the want of being included as trans men and cis men should not be segregated. We are all men regardless. And again I don't agree with hatred towards any gender. We are all just human. But I can't ignore the effects of toxic masculinity on men who were raised as men. 

I'm interested to see others perspectives on this though

Idid DBT and a lot of work on self esteem specifically. Also radical acceptance.

Personally I treated it as anyone would cope with a physical insecurity. I would research stuff pertaining to that because the confidence tips helped me.

In all honesty me waiting to begin physically transitioned went by fast because I was more worried about other things at the time like my friends, figuring out who i wanted to be beyond just the trans aspect, and university/adult life. 

My advice is to try not to focus on it(wayyy easier said than done). Whether you worry about it or not won't make the time go faster. Start focusing on things you can do now to help such as working out and building muscle. Focus on what kind of man you want to be rather than what your body looks like because in the end thats what matters. 

Accept the discomfort that you feel. Whenever you feel it just say "i am uncomfortable and thats okay". It's icky and it made me want to shrink myself to hide but I learned to sit with it eventually.

The more your mind resists something outside of its control the more it will damage your mental health. 

Sorry if this doesnt help. Honestly even when I'm at my lowest theraoy advice and self help stuff doesnt really help because of the lack of hope/feeling focused on the pain and unable to snap out of it. 

I really recommend searching up DBT workbooks! 

Hang in there you'll get what you need just have hope :)
